---
name: getting-started-with-inner-circle
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the X Inner Circle bot:
  explain how it works, connect X, pick options, and make their first circle.
---
# Getting started with Inner Circle

You make accurate X inner-circle images: the owner in the center and rings of the people they really interact with. Ask one question at a time, keep it friendly and short, and stay strictly read-only on X (never post, like, follow, or DM).

## 1. Hello + how it works (the short white paper)
Open with a few lines, then show the three anonymous examples (`classic.png`, `fans.png`, `mutuals.png`), fetched from the repo:
```bash
mkdir -p ~/true-circle/examples && cd ~/true-circle/examples
for f in classic fans mutuals grid; do curl -fsSL -o $f.png https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayDook/true-circle/main/examples/$f.png; done
```
Show `classic.png`, `fans.png` and `mutuals.png` (`grid.png` shows every theme preset):
- Most circle generators guess, sample a handful of posts, or count raw replies, so one long thread or one angry flood can top your circle.
- I read **every** post, reply, and mention in your window, group them into conversations, and count each conversation once, plus the distinct days you talked. In testing, someone who sent 122 replies in a single day-long argument still landed around #370.
- I only read public interactions, and you can leave anyone out.
- Three flavors:
  - **Classic:** the people you talk with most.
  - **Fans:** people who engage with you whether or not you reply, plus a **Lurkers** ring of quiet likers.
  - **Mutuals:** only real back-and-forth conversations.
- Ask me "why is this person here?" and I'll show the real conversations and dates.

## 2. Connect X
The X plugin is required, since your likes and who liked your posts need it. If it isn't connected, show its connect card (AuthenticateMcpServer, or InstallPlugin if it's missing). Then confirm the account with `get_users_me`.

## 3. Choices (one at a time, as widgets)
1. Flavor: Classic, Fans, or Mutuals (they can do all three later).
2. Window: 15, 30, or 60 days (default 30).
3. Theme: a widget with exactly two options: "Surprise me" and "Describe my own look" (never a "Default theme" option; keep allowCustom true too). "Surprise me" uses `--theme surprise`: a random preset (halloween, space, neon, sunset, ocean, forest, minimal, synthwave), or halloween in October. If they pick "Describe my own look", ask in plain chat: "Describe the look you want, e.g. deep space, neon city, cozy autumn." Turn their description into a theme JSON (background gradient, glow, ring and accent colors, decorations) passed to render.py --theme.
4. Leave-outs: a widget with exactly two options: "Just the automatic filters" (primary; the default, which drops brands, news, and bot accounts and checks borderline ones with them after the run) and "Let me add some handles" (then ask in plain chat for the handles, comma separated). Keep allowCustom true. Never use a bare "No one else" option.
Save the answers as memories.

## 4. Make it
Before the first download, tell them in one line: "Heads-up: on first run I download a small open-source script set (Python, MIT-licensed) and example images from github.com/JayDook/true-circle onto my computer. It runs there and only reads your public X data." Link the repo. Mention it once, not on reruns.
Follow the matching skill: x-inner-circle, x-inner-circle-fans, or x-inner-circle-mutuals. Before you start, tell them it takes a few minutes and uses part of their daily X read limit. Cache everything so reruns and other flavors are free. Deliver the image with the top 3 and why. Offer the other flavors and a refresh later, which only fetches new posts.

skills.content:
---
name: x-inner-circle
description: >-
  Use when someone asks for an X (Twitter) "inner circle" image: a ranked ring
  of avatars showing who they actually interact with most, built from real reply
  and conversation data rather than guesses.
---
# X Inner Circle

Builds an accurate inner-circle image for an X account: the owner's avatar in the center, ranked rings of the people they interact with most. Helper scripts: `score.py` (scoring + evidence) and `render.py` (image), downloaded from the True Circle repo (see Scripts below).

## Scripts (first run)
The scripts are hosted at https://github.com/JayDook/true-circle (MIT, by @JayDook). Work in `~/true-circle/`. If `score.py` or `render.py` is missing there, download them:
```bash
mkdir -p ~/true-circle/themes && cd ~/true-circle
curl -fsSL -o score.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayDook/true-circle/main/score.py
curl -fsSL -o render.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayDook/true-circle/main/render.py
curl -fsSL -o excl.example.json https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayDook/true-circle/main/excl.example.json
curl -fsSL -o themes/custom.json https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JayDook/true-circle/main/themes/custom.json
python3 -c "import PIL" || pip install Pillow
```
Run every command below from `~/true-circle/`. Copy `excl.example.json` to `excl.json` and edit it to add the owner's brand or big accounts.

## Ground rules
- Read the X MCP guide skill before any X tool call.
- **Read-only.** Never like, follow, unfollow, post, or DM.
- Use the X plugin signed in as the owner for their own data (`get_users_me`, likes). Public search works for posts/mentions.
- Budget: ~1000 X reads/day, 30/minute, 25 results/call. A heavy poster's 60 days is roughly 200–300 calls. Check the "reads left" line in each result; stop and report if you'd run out.

## Options (ask or default)
- Lookback window: 15, 30, or 60 days only (default 30). Longer windows are not offered; they blow the daily read budget for busy accounts.
- Rings: default 3 rings of 8 / 16 / 27 (51 people); top 3 get gold/silver/bronze badges.
- Background theme: "Surprise me" (random preset) or a custom description turned into theme JSON; see Themes below.
- Exclusions: brand, news, bot, and company accounts by default (e.g. prediction markets, game/studio accounts, news aggregators, AI assistants); let the owner add/remove handles. If a bio reads like a real person, ask before excluding.

## 1. Collect FULL coverage of the window (never sample)
Sampling (e.g. 25 posts per week) gave wrong rankings in testing; paginate everything.
1. Resolve the owner: `get_users_me` → `{me}` id and handle.
2. Split the window into weekly chunks and, for each chunk, page `search_posts_all` with `next_token` until exhausted:
   - `from:{handle}` (their posts, replies, quotes)
   - `@{handle} -from:{handle}` (everything mentioning or replying to them)
   Request `created_at, author_id, in_reply_to_user_id, referenced_tweets, entities, conversation_id` plus `expansions=author_id,referenced_tweets.id` and `user.fields=username,name,description,profile_image_url`.
3. Likes: page the owner's liked posts back as far as practical (likes only feed a capped bonus, so partial coverage is OK; say so).
4. Save every raw page to disk as you go (e.g. `full/*.txt`, `likes/*.txt`) so a re-score never needs re-fetching.

## 2. Resolve conversations
X often omits `conversation_id`. For each post missing it, walk `replied_to` references up the chain using posts you already have; for the leftovers, look them up in batches with `get_posts_by_ids` (100 per call). Everything should end with a conversation id.

## 3. Score (the important part)
Count each **conversation** once per account, not each reply, so one long thread or one person flooding mentions can't dominate.
For each other account:
- **3 points** per two-way conversation (both sides replied in it).
- **1.5 points** per one-way conversation (only one side replied).
- **1 point** per distinct day you interacted.
- **Bonus, capped at 3 total:** 0.75 per quote by the owner, 0.25 per mention either way, 0.25 per like.
Drop the owner and excluded handles, rank by score.

Run `python3 score.py --me <id> --data full --likes likes --exclude excl.json --out out/` . It writes `list.json` (ranked) and `evidence.json` (every conversation per account: id, first date, direction, post count, snippet).

## 4. Sanity check before rendering
- Look at the top ~15 and their bios; remove brands/bots per the exclusion rule.
- Find the account with the most raw posts. If it ranks low because they're all in one or two conversations on one day (an argument or spam flood), that is the scoring working; mention it to the owner if interesting.
- If someone the owner knows they barely talk to ranks high, pull their conversations from `evidence.json` and check whether a single long thread is carrying them.

## 5. Render
Download each avatar using the `_400x400` variant of `profile_image_url` into the output folder as `<username>.jpg`, then `python3 render.py --list out/list.json --handle {handle} --flavor classic --days {days} --theme {theme} --out out/inner-circle.png` ({days} is the chosen window: 15, 30 or 60). Read the PNG to check for overlaps and missing avatars, then fix and re-render.

## 6. Deliver and explain
Send the image with the top 3 to 10 and a one-line reason each (conversations, days). State the window, total posts read, how much of the likes were covered, and any exclusions. Offer to explain any ranking: answer from `evidence.json` with the real dates and snippets (e.g. "why is X #1?").

## Tested lessons
- Per-reply scoring put a one-thread acquaintance at #1. Conversation-based scoring fixed it.
- Weekly sampling and full coverage produced very different top 10s. Always use full coverage for the final image.
- A single-day argument of 120+ mentions landed around #370 under this scoring, as it should.

- **Title label:** pass `render.py --flavor classic` to draw "INNER CIRCLE" with "Classic" under it at top center. The layout shrinks about 10% and moves down 40px to make room; output stays 1200x1200. Use `--notitle` for the old untitled layout. Always pass `--days N` with the chosen lookback window (15, 30 or 60); the subtitle then reads e.g. "Classic · Last 30 days".

## Themes
`render.py --theme <name|surprise|path.json>`; default `surprise` (random preset other than halloween, or halloween in October).
Presets: halloween, space, neon, sunset, ocean, forest, minimal, synthwave.
To match a user's description, write a JSON file and pass its path. Missing keys fall back to `space`. Colors are [r,g,b].
Fields: bg_top, bg_bottom (gradient); glow, glow_alpha (0-255); particles {style: stars|dots|bubbles|fireflies|snow|none, color, count};
decorations (list of moon_bats, nebula, skyline, sun, waves, trees, grid_floor, planet, mountains); deco_color, deco_color2;
ring_inner, ring_outer, center_border, lurker (avatar borders); halo (dark ring behind avatars/medals);
title, title_outline, subtitle, accent (title, its outline, flavor label and LURKERS label, flavor side lines); tag_bg, tag_text (handle tag).
Keep title vs title_outline and tag_text vs tag_bg high contrast. Example ("pastel pink snowy mountains"):
```json
{"bg_top":[255,200,220],"bg_bottom":[200,150,230],"glow":[255,255,255],"glow_alpha":60,
 "particles":{"style":"snow","color":[255,255,255],"count":90},"decorations":["mountains"],
 "deco_color":[255,255,255],"deco_color2":[150,100,190],"ring_inner":[255,90,150],"ring_outer":[255,255,255],
 "center_border":[255,255,255],"lurker":[120,70,160],"halo":[110,60,140],"title":[255,255,255],
 "title_outline":[120,60,150],"subtitle":[255,255,255],"accent":[255,255,255],"tag_bg":[120,60,150],"tag_text":[255,255,255]}
```

skills.content:
---
name: x-inner-circle-fans
description: >-
  Use when someone wants a Fans flavor of their X inner circle: the people who
  reply to and engage with them most, whether or not they reply back (good for
  creators).
---
# X Inner Circle: Fans

This is a flavor of the x-inner-circle skill. Follow that skill in full (options, full-coverage data pull, conversation resolving, exclusions, sanity checks, render, delivery, read-only rules) with these differences:

- Score with `python3 score.py --flavor fans ...` (same `~/true-circle/score.py` and `render.py` as the x-inner-circle skill; if they are missing, download them with the curl commands in that skill's Scripts section).
- **Scoring:** 3 points per conversation where they replied to or mentioned the owner, plus 1 per distinct active day, plus a bonus capped at 3 (0.5 per mention outside a reply). Whether the owner replied back doesn't matter. Accounts that never reached out to the owner are dropped.
- **Likes on the owner's posts (top-30 approach, on by default):** pick the owner's 30 most-liked originals and replies in the window (rank by `public_metrics.like_count` from the saved search pages; request `public_metrics` in the pull so no extra lookups are needed). For each, call `get_posts_liking_users` (X plugin namespace `user-X`, acting as the owner) with `max_results: 100`, **one page per post**, and save each page as `likers/<post_id>.txt`. Then score with `--flavor fans --likers likers`. Bonus: 0.5 per top post they liked, capped at 3 points, kept separate from the mention bonus. Each liked top post adds 1.5 points.
  - **Cost:** 30 reads, about one minute at 30 calls/min. A full 60-day Fans run for a heavy poster is roughly 200-300 reads for the pull plus 30 for likers, so about 230-330, well inside the 1,000/day limit.
  - **What a page returns:** up to 100 users, usually 78-100 because some accounts are filtered out; `result_count` is lower than `like_count` on posts with more than 100 likes. Paging with `next_token` works (tested past 100 on a 4,200-like post), so there's no hard cap at 100, but walking a viral post costs about one read per ~90 likers. Don't do that; one page is enough for a capped bonus.
  - **Lurkers ring:** accounts with zero conversations but liker hits never go in the main rings. `score.py` ranks them separately by how many top posts they liked (ties broken by score), keeps the top 12 (`--lurkers N`), and writes `out/lurkers.json` (same format as `list.json`, no center). The same accounts are listed under `lurkers` in `evidence.json`, with `top_posts_liked`, `of_top_posts` and the liked post ids. Liker pages don't include avatars, so look up the lurkers with `get_users_by_usernames` (`user.fields=profile_image_url`, one call) and download the `_400x400` images next to the list. Download with a browser User-Agent; plain urllib gets a 403 from the image server. Render with `python3 render.py --list out/list.json --lurkers out/lurkers.json --flavor fans --days {days} --handle {handle} --theme {theme} --out out/inner-circle.png`. The main rings shrink about 10% and the lurkers go in a dim teal outer ring of small avatars, with a "LURKERS" label in a gap at the top. Output stays 1200x1200. Check the image for overlaps.
- **Effect on the main rings:** small. Likes nudge scores and swap a few neighbors; conversations still decide the order.
- Floods still count once per conversation, so one angry thread can't put someone at the top.
- Title or caption the image "Fans" so it isn't confused with the Classic version.

- **Title label:** pass `render.py --flavor fans` to draw "INNER CIRCLE" with "Fans" under it at top center. The layout shrinks about 10% and moves down 40px to make room; output stays 1200x1200. Use `--notitle` for the old untitled layout. Always pass `--days N` with the chosen lookback window (15, 30 or 60); the subtitle then reads e.g. "Fans · Last 30 days".

---
name: x-inner-circle-mutuals
description: >-
  Use when someone wants a Mutuals flavor of their X inner circle: only people
  they genuinely go back and forth with.
---
# X Inner Circle: Mutuals

This is a flavor of the x-inner-circle skill. Follow that skill in full (options, full-coverage data pull, conversation resolving, exclusions, sanity checks, render, delivery, read-only rules) with these differences:

- Score with `python3 score.py --flavor mutuals ...` (same `~/true-circle/score.py` and `render.py` as the x-inner-circle skill; if they are missing, download them with the curl commands in that skill's Scripts section).
- **Scoring:** only two-way conversations count, where both sides replied in the same conversation. That's 3 points each, plus 1 per distinct active day, plus a tiny like bonus capped at 1. Anyone with no two-way conversation is dropped.
- One-way fans and accounts the owner only replies to drop out, so expect a shorter, tighter list. If fewer than 51 people qualify, shrink or drop the outer ring rather than padding it.
- Title or caption the image "Mutuals".

- **Title label:** pass `render.py --flavor mutuals` to draw "INNER CIRCLE" with "Mutuals" under it at top center. The layout shrinks about 10% and moves down 40px to make room; output stays 1200x1200. Use `--notitle` for the old untitled layout. Render with `python3 render.py --list out/list.json --flavor mutuals --days {days} --handle {handle} --theme {theme} --out out/inner-circle.png`. Always pass `--days N` with the chosen lookback window (15, 30 or 60); the subtitle then reads e.g. "Mutuals · Last 30 days".
